reviewStatus: Drafted from verified sources; pending independent clinician review before clinical release.

consistencyRules.message: 'Undetermined' already covers incomplete or conflicting evaluation; probable/possible applies to the other subtypes.

commonErrors: Assigning small-vessel occlusion to a subcortical infarct over 1.5 cm.
Assigning a subtype before vascular and cardiac evaluation is complete without marking it 'possible'.
name: TOAST Classification of Ischaemic Stroke Subtype

version.label: TOAST (Adams et al. 1993), five subtypes
version.detail: Each subtype may be graded 'probable' or 'possible' depending on how complete and consistent the investigations are. Later systems (e.g. SSS-TOAST, ASCOD) are different versions and are not combined.

purpose: Classifies ischaemic stroke by presumed mechanism, using clinical features and investigations.
intendedPopulation: Adults with ischaemic stroke after vascular, cardiac and laboratory investigation.

calculatorNotice.title: Assign after investigation
calculatorNotice.message: TOAST depends on vascular imaging, cardiac evaluation and other tests. Assigned early, it is often provisional.

options.label: Large-artery atherosclerosis
options.detail: Significant (>50%) stenosis or occlusion of a major brain artery or branch cortical artery, presumed atherosclerotic; cortical, cerebellar, brainstem or large (>1.5 cm) subcortical infarct; cardioembolic source excluded.

options.label: Cardioembolism
options.detail: Arterial occlusion presumed due to an embolus from the heart; at least one cardiac source of embolism identified.

options.label: Small-vessel occlusion (lacune)
options.detail: Classical lacunar syndrome; normal imaging or a relevant brainstem or subcortical lesion under 1.5 cm; no cardiac source or ipsilateral large-artery stenosis over 50%.

options.label: Stroke of other determined aetiology
options.detail: Rare causes, e.g. non-atherosclerotic vasculopathy, hypercoagulable state or haematological disorder, with investigations supporting it.

options.label: Stroke of undetermined aetiology
options.detail: Two or more possible causes, a negative evaluation, or an incomplete evaluation.

options.label: Probable
options.detail: Clinical findings, imaging and investigations consistent; other causes excluded.

options.label: Possible
options.detail: Clinical and imaging findings suggest the subtype but investigations are incomplete.

clinicalContext.text: Classifies ischaemic stroke by presumed mechanism, which guides secondary prevention and research grouping.
The most widely used stroke subtype classification in trials.

clinicalInsights.text: Undetermined includes cryptogenic stroke after full evaluation and strokes with two competing causes; say which.
Record which investigations were complete; the subtype can change as results arrive.

limitations.text: Assignment depends on how complete the investigations are; 'undetermined' rises when evaluation is limited.

limitations: Does not separate embolic stroke of undetermined source as its own group.

confounders.effect: e.g. atrial fibrillation with carotid stenosis.

guideSections.what: Five ischaemic stroke subtypes by presumed mechanism: large-artery atherosclerosis, cardioembolism, small-vessel occlusion, other determined and undetermined.
guideSections.whenToUse: After investigation of ischaemic stroke; communication, secondary prevention planning and research.
guideSections.howToPerform: Combine the clinical syndrome, brain imaging, vascular imaging, cardiac evaluation and laboratory tests. Choose the subtype, then mark probable or possible.
guideSections.clinicalContext: A mechanism classification, used with the full investigation results.

sources.citation: Adams HP Jr, Bendixen BH, Kappelle LJ, et al. Classification of subtype of acute ischemic stroke. Definitions for use in a multicenter clinical trial. TOAST. Trial of Org 10172 in Acute Stroke Treatment. Stroke. 1993;24(1):35-41.
